1046: The three-way interaction was highly significant. Among the thirty six treatment combinations, the maximum value of 69.63 mg TE/100 g was recorded by Kalojira grown at Birbhum/Howrah and sampled as fresh paddy, and the minimum of 10.42 mg TE/100 g by Gobindabhog grown at Purba Bardhaman and sampled at 12 months, a spread of 59.21 mg TE/100 g. This range appreciably exceeded that generated by any single factor in isolation, the three factors having operated jointly; a favourable outcome therefore required all three to be specified concurrently.
1055: Antioxidant capacity quantifies the efficacy with which a grain extract neutralises free radicals. Grain from Birbhum and Howrah accordingly represents the preferred provenance among the three for those valuing aromatic rice on account of its health-promoting properties. Had phenolics alone been responsible, antioxidant capacity could not have declined more rapidly than they did. Since Birbhum and Howrah also commenced from the highest baseline, the margin between locations widened over the year rather than converging. Naveed et al. (2023) stored five brown Basmati varieties for three and six months at 5 and 25 °C and observed that antioxidant activity declined by up to 50%, the loss increasing with both duration and temperature, while oleic and linoleic acids were concurrently depleted. With respect to location, Kunnam et al. (2023) evaluated six rice genotypes at three sites in Thailand and identified environment as the principal source of variation in total phenolic content and antioxidant capacity, although certain genotypes maintained their values consistently across sites.
1060: Location exerted a highly significant effect on phytic acid. The highest value, 339.23 mg/100 g, was recorded at Birbhum/Howrah, followed by Purba Bardhaman with 283.61 mg/100 g and Nadia with 216.14 mg/100 g. Each location occupied a discrete letter group, matching neither of the others, and the gap between the superior and inferior sites amounted to 123.09 mg/100 g.
1062: The three landraces likewise differed, the varietal effect being highly significant. Gobindabhog recorded the highest value, 336.04 mg/100 g, followed by Radhunipagal with 306.86 mg/100 g and Kalojira with 196.07 mg/100 g. The three landraces resolved into discrete groups, Gobindabhog exceeding Kalojira by 139.97 mg/100 g.
1064: Storage period altered phytic acid to a highly significant degree. In order of sampling, the values were 350.10 mg/100 g in fresh paddy, 309.79 mg/100 g at 4 months, 248.66 mg/100 g at 8 months and 210.08 mg/100 g at 12 months, fresh paddy returning the highest value and 12 months the lowest. By the close of the year the value had declined by 40.0%.
1066: The location × variety interaction was highly significant. Gobindabhog at Birbhum/Howrah constituted the superior combination with 460.67 mg/100 g, and Kalojira at Birbhum/Howrah the inferior one with 175.02 mg/100 g. The varietal order was not conserved across sites: at Nadia the sequence ran Gobindabhog, Kalojira, Radhunipagal; at Purba Bardhaman, Radhunipagal, Gobindabhog, Kalojira; and at Birbhum/Howrah, Gobindabhog, Radhunipagal, Kalojira. Rank reversal of this order establishes that the landraces responded differentially to the three environments.
1067: Location and storage did not interact significantly. The highest mean, 409.95 mg/100 g, was recorded for Birbhum/Howrah in fresh paddy and the lowest, 144.22 mg/100 g, for Nadia at 12 months. Over 12 months of storage the change amounted to -49.9% at Nadia, -36.8% at Purba Bardhaman and -35.8% at Birbhum/Howrah. The three locations shifted by nearly equivalent margins, the district of production exerting negligible influence on the action of storage.
1068: The variety × storage interaction was significant at the 1% level. The highest mean, 408.86 mg/100 g, was recorded for Gobindabhog in fresh paddy and the lowest, 139.17 mg/100 g, for Kalojira at 12 months. Over the year Gobindabhog changed by -35.5%, Radhunipagal by -41.3% and Kalojira by -45.2%, Kalojira shifting furthest and Gobindabhog least. The three landraces consequently did not gain or lose at equivalent rates during storage.
1069: The three-factor interaction attained the 1% level. Among the thirty six treatment combinations, the maximum value of 513.34 mg/100 g was recorded by Gobindabhog grown at Birbhum/Howrah and sampled as fresh paddy, and the minimum of 131.60 mg/100 g by Gobindabhog grown at Nadia and sampled at 12 months, a spread of 381.74 mg/100 g. No single factor in isolation generated a range of this width; location, landrace and storage acted in combination, and the optimum outcome was attainable only through the appropriate conjunction of all three.
1078: Phytic acid is an anti-nutrient that chelates iron and zinc and thereby renders them unavailable for absorption in the human gut. This is a consideration of considerable weight in a country where rice is the staple and iron and zinc deficiencies are prevalent. From a nutritional standpoint the low value recorded at Nadia is the desirable one, since a reduced phytic acid content implies greater bioavailability of grain iron and zinc. Gobindabhog carried substantially more phytic acid than Kalojira, and the same order obtained at all three locations, which indicates that the difference is genetic in origin. A breeder may therefore select for reduced phytate without recourse to induced mutants. No previous study of this character in these landraces, or of its change during storage, was identified among the literature reviewed in Chapter II, so the present values may be regarded as a first record for the cultivars concerned.
1083: Location exerted a highly significant effect on the L* value. The highest value, 76.59, was recorded at Purba Bardhaman, followed by Nadia with 74.77 and Birbhum/Howrah with 74.23. All three locations were statistically discrete, differing significantly among themselves, and the gap between the superior and inferior sites amounted to 2.36.
1085: The landraces likewise differed significantly, the varietal effect being highly significant. Radhunipagal recorded the highest value, 75.74, followed by Gobindabhog with 75.40 and Kalojira with 74.44. No two landraces shared a letter group, Radhunipagal exceeding Kalojira by 1.30.
1087: Storage period altered the L* value significantly at the 1% level. In order of sampling, the values were 75.02 in fresh paddy, 75.38 at 4 months, 75.00 at 8 months and 75.39 at 12 months, the maximum occurring at 12 months and the minimum at 8 months. Over the full year the value increased by 0.5%.
1089: The location × variety interaction was significant at the 1% level. Radhunipagal at Purba Bardhaman constituted the superior combination with 77.51, and Kalojira at Birbhum/Howrah the inferior one with 72.23. Varietal ranking was not conserved across the three districts: Nadia yielded the order Radhunipagal, Kalojira, Gobindabhog; Purba Bardhaman the order Radhunipagal, Kalojira, Gobindabhog; and Birbhum/Howrah the order Gobindabhog, Radhunipagal, Kalojira. Such rank reversal establishes that the three environments did not act uniformly upon every landrace.
1090: Location and storage period acted jointly. The highest mean, 76.85, was recorded for Purba Bardhaman at 12 months and the lowest, 73.84, for Birbhum/Howrah at 8 months. Between fresh paddy and 12 months of storage the change amounted to +1.4% at Nadia, +0.1% at Purba Bardhaman and -0.0% at Birbhum/Howrah. The magnitude of change scarcely differed between locations, storage having elicited an equivalent response in grain of all three provenances.
1091: The variety × storage interaction was highly significant. The highest mean, 75.83, was recorded for Radhunipagal at 8 months and the lowest, 74.05, for Kalojira in fresh paddy. Over the twelve months the change amounted to +0.2% in Gobindabhog, +0.2% in Radhunipagal and +1.1% in Kalojira. The magnitude of change was comparable in all three landraces, storage having acted upon them equivalently.
1092: The three factors interacted significantly. Among the thirty six treatment combinations, the maximum value of 79.71 was recorded by Radhunipagal grown at Purba Bardhaman and sampled as fresh paddy, and the minimum of 71.80 by Kalojira grown at Birbhum/Howrah and sampled at 4 months, a spread of 7.91. This range far exceeded that attributable to any factor in isolation; the effect proceeded from the three factors in conjunction, and all three required appropriate specification to secure the optimum outcome.
1101: The L* value expresses the brightness of the milled rice. Surface brightness after polishing is contingent upon the smoothness and translucency of the kernel, both of which are established during grain filling. A high L* is therefore not invariably indicative of superior quality, and the brightness recorded there may reflect a chalkier endosperm rather than more effective polishing. The same landrace also returned the highest phenol, flavonoid and antioxidant readings in this study, which is consistent, since those pigments are themselves phenolic compounds; Zhang et al. (2010) described an equivalent pigment load in the bran of black rice. Yanxia et al. (2018) arrived at the same conclusion for milled rice held at room temperature, reporting only a marginal change in L*. Colour, therefore, does not appear to be the attribute limiting the storage life of these landraces.
1105: Location exerted a highly significant effect on the a* value. The highest value, -1.154, was recorded at Nadia, followed by Birbhum/Howrah with -1.222 and Purba Bardhaman with -2.208. Nadia and Birbhum/Howrah shared a common letter group, the difference between them being too small to be regarded as real, while the gap between the superior and inferior locations amounted to 1.054.
1107: The three landraces likewise differed, the varietal effect being highly significant. Kalojira recorded the highest value, -0.702, followed by Radhunipagal with -1.630 and Gobindabhog with -2.252. The three landraces resolved into discrete groups, Kalojira exceeding Gobindabhog by 1.550.
1109: Storage period altered the a* value significantly at the 1% level. In order of sampling, the values were -3.310 in fresh paddy, -0.764 at 4 months, -1.176 at 8 months and -0.862 at 12 months, the maximum occurring at 4 months and the minimum in fresh paddy. Across the twelve months the value declined by 74.0%.
1111: The location × variety interaction was highly significant. Kalojira at Birbhum/Howrah constituted the superior combination with 1.325, and Gobindabhog at Birbhum/Howrah the inferior one with -4.563. The landraces did not retain the same order at every location: the order at Nadia was Gobindabhog, Kalojira, Radhunipagal; at Purba Bardhaman, Gobindabhog, Kalojira, Radhunipagal; and at Birbhum/Howrah, Kalojira, Radhunipagal, Gobindabhog. Rank reversal of this kind indicates a differential response to the growing environment.
1112: The location × storage interaction was significant at the 1% level. The highest mean, 0.138, was recorded for Birbhum/Howrah at 4 months and the lowest, -4.548, for Purba Bardhaman in fresh paddy. Between harvest and 12 months the change amounted to -0.6% at Nadia, -72.6% at Purba Bardhaman and -95.2% at Birbhum/Howrah, a spread of 94.6 percentage points, with grain from Birbhum/Howrah changing most and that from Nadia least. The rate of change during storage was therefore not uniform across grain of the three provenances.
1113: The variety × storage interaction attained the 1% level. The highest mean, -0.499, was recorded for Kalojira at 12 months and the lowest, -4.885, for Gobindabhog in fresh paddy. Twelve months of storage yielded changes of -76.3% in Gobindabhog, -79.0% in Radhunipagal and -18.5% in Kalojira, Radhunipagal shifting furthest and Kalojira least. The three landraces therefore did not gain or lose at equivalent rates during storage.
1114: The L × V × S interaction was highly significant. Among the thirty six treatment combinations, the maximum value of 1.790 was recorded by Kalojira grown at Birbhum/Howrah and sampled at 12 months, and the minimum of -13.290 by Gobindabhog grown at Birbhum/Howrah and sampled as fresh paddy, a spread of 15.080. This range substantially exceeded that attributable to any individual factor; all three factors operated jointly, and the optimum outcome was contingent upon the correct specification of each.
1123: The a* value locates a sample on the green-to-red axis. This accords with the brighter, chalkier grain recorded at Purba Bardhaman, since incompletely filled grain tends to retain more of its immature pigment. Kalojira consequently lay closest to neutral even in the fresh condition. The same pigments account for the highest ranking of Kalojira for phenol, flavonoid and antioxidant capacity in this study, and explain the greenish cast frequently exhibited by freshly milled rice, which dissipates after the first storage season. Those same reactions may explain the steep decline in extractable phenol content observed here, and Zhou et al. (2004) reported a comparable loss of phenolic acids in stored rice. The explanation lies in the fact that Kalojira commenced much closer to neutral and therefore possessed less green pigment to forfeit. Since the grand mean is negative, the coefficient of variation likewise prints as a negative figure and should be read as 14.19%.
